manualPage.pageSub: Reference guide: 4 service types · pipeline stages · how to handle 8 special situations
manualPage.section3Title: 8 special situations — how to handle them
manualPage.ciDesc: Customer brings the device to the center themselves. Repaired at the center, then returned.
manualPage.stDesc: Company/warehouse device. Repaired at the center.
manualPage.ihDesc: Technician goes to repair at home. Device never comes to the center — finished on site.
manualPage.psName: Pick up device to repair at the center
manualPage.psDesc: Pick up device at customer's home → repair at center → return.
manualPage.pipelineIntroA: Every repair ticket flows through stages 1–12. PS and IH have a
manualPage.pipelineIntroB: of their own before entering stage 1.
manualPage.stageNoteB: (quotation) only happen when out of warranty · stages
manualPage.stageNoteC: (parts) only happen when parts are needed. In warranty + no parts → skip to stage 8.
manualPage.ihFlowB: (CS, must enter appointment date) → tech goes (check-in GPS) → inspect + repair → QC → close (no “return”)
manualPage.sit1Title: IH can't be repaired on site → bring into center
manualPage.sit1Sit: Technician arrived at the home but can't repair on site (needs center tools / deeper inspection).
manualPage.sit1Step1: Technician taps “Can't repair on site — bring into center” in the app (during stage 1–2) with a reason
manualPage.sit1Step2: The job converts to PS automatically → enters the “picking up” queue
manualPage.sit1Step3: CS taps “Receive into center” when the device arrives → inspect + repair at center → return
manualPage.sit1Note: Once it becomes PS, it automatically gets a “return” stage (the device must be delivered back to the customer).
manualPage.sit2Title: IH needs to order parts (no stock)
manualPage.sit2Sit: Inspection found that a part not in stock is needed. Decide during inspection:
manualPage.sit2Step1: Want to repair at center → tap “Bring into center” first (becomes PS) → order per the flow → part arrives → repair at center
manualPage.sit2Step2: Want to repair on site → don't bring in, order the part → part arrives (stage 8) → schedule the tech for a second visit
manualPage.sit2Note: The purchasing mechanism (stage 7) works the same — the only difference is whether it's brought into the center or a second visit.
manualPage.sit3Sit: The person who inspects and the person who will repair are different people.
manualPage.sit3Step2: CS/Supervisor opens the ticket at /service/<number> → taps “Change technician” to B
manualPage.sit3Step3: Technician B accepts the job (in the app) and continues the repair
manualPage.sit3Note: You can't change technician after parts have been requested (the request was issued under A). Labor pay goes to whoever closes the job (B).
manualPage.sit4Sit: Started the repair (stage 9) and found you need more parts or the wrong one. The job stays in “repairing”.
manualPage.sit4Step1: Web: on /service/<number>, in the “parts during repair” box — search + add / remove
manualPage.sit4Step2: App: the “Request / swap parts (during repair)” button
manualPage.sit4Step3: Tap “Request more parts” → issue a second parts request → warehouse issues them
manualPage.sit4Note: Swapping a part = return the old one + add the new one. A row already issued (locked) can't be removed.
manualPage.sit5Title: Cancel a job with outstanding parts
manualPage.sit5Sit: You want to close the job as cancelled, but parts issued for use (inspection/repair) haven't been returned.
manualPage.sit5Step1: The system won't let you close for free if there are outstanding parts (shows a warning)
manualPage.sit5Step2: Choose 1 of 2: return the parts (parts recovery page) or issue a receipt to charge for the parts
manualPage.sit5Step3: Then you can close the job / return the device to the customer
manualPage.sit5Note: Closes an old leak: a cancellation closed while parts were never returned ⇒ stock ends up lower than reality.
manualPage.sit6Title: Transfer parts to the repair room (no issue)
manualPage.sit6Sit: You want the parts at the repair room but still as stock (not deducted/not billed to a job).
manualPage.sit6Step1: Go to the Warehouse menu → “Request transfer of parts to repair room”
manualPage.sit6Step2: Choose the repair-room warehouse (1104 Khua Luang / 1206 Don Tiu) + search/add parts → create a transfer request
manualPage.sit6Step3: The main warehouse issues the actual transfer (FT) in ERP → tap “Receive” at Transfer tracking
manualPage.sit6Note: A transfer request doesn't deduct stock — it's a request for the main warehouse to transfer. Different from an “issue”, which deducts stock to a job.
manualPage.sit7Sit: You want to try fitting a part to diagnose (may or may not actually use it).
manualPage.sit7Step1: During inspection, add the part to the list and try it
manualPage.sit7Step2: Actually used → keep it on the list (proceed to issue)
manualPage.sit7Step3: Not used → remove it (before issuing) or return to warehouse (after issuing)
manualPage.sit7Note: Use the existing add/remove/return mechanism — no special marking needed.
manualPage.sit8Sit: Count the customer devices that should actually be in the center (stages 1–11).
manualPage.sit8Step1: Open the Warehouse menu → Stock count (web = table · mobile = scan)
manualPage.sit8Step2: Scan the device's barcode / SN — once found it's marked automatically
manualPage.sit8Note: IH is skipped (at the customer's home) · PS is counted only once received into the center.
manualPage.role1Duty: Receive into center (PS) · set appointment + assign tech (IH) · change tech · cancel · issue receipt
manualPage.role2Duty: Accept job · inspect · check-in/out GPS · repair · bring into center · request/swap parts
manualPage.role4Duty: Issue parts · transfer to repair room · receive transfers · receive returned parts · track inventory
manualPage.role5Duty: Pick up device at customer's home (PS) · deliver device back

extraSections.title: Stock count & not-found devices
extraSections.intro: The “Repair stock count” page (Warehouse & Spares menu) — managers/approvers scan a barcode or type a job no./SN to count devices physically present in the center.
items: Scan a barcode or type job no./SN → instantly marked “found”, with a beep (found = high, duplicate = double, not-found = low).
Any job can be counted, not just pending — if you see it, count it. Scanning again says “already counted”.
Cancel one count: click 🗑 on the row → confirm → the count record is removed (you can re-scan).
Genuinely missing devices: go to the count report → “Not counted” tab → click “Close · not found” → confirm → the job moves to “Not found / missing”.
Once closed, the job leaves the pending queue everywhere (/service, dashboard, pipeline, pending report) — no data deleted, ERP untouched.
Undo: the “Not-found devices (missing)” menu (or the same tab) → click “Restore” → the job returns to the pending queue.
Report: “Stock count results” — summary of to-count / found / not-counted / missing, split by tab and by service (CI/ST/IH/PS), Excel export.

extraSections.title: Tracking label & barcode
extraSections.intro: Print a 75 × 100 mm sticker to attach to the customer's device for tracking.
items: Open the label: on /service (table or board) click the 🏷 icon, or on the count page click 🖶 — opens /service/[job]/label.
The label has: service-center info, device details (product/brand/model/SN/customer/symptom/accessories/stage), a Code128 barcode of the job number, and a tracking QR.
QR → /track/<job> (public, no login) — the customer can scan to check status themselves.
Print: click “Print tracking label” → choose 75×100 paper size or use a thermal label printer.
The A4 receipt (orange 🖨) is unchanged — the sticker (75×100) is the new device tag.

extraSections.title: Reports & settings
items: Key reports (Reports menu): performance KPI, backlog, daily intake, receipts, repeat repairs, stock-count results, and more.
Excel: many pages have a “Export / Excel” button — output matches the on-screen filters.
System settings (manager): Users → System settings — toggle features like “Manage backlog” (needs-check/cancel/repaired) and “Notify all activity”.
Access rights: Users → Permissions — set which menus each employee can see/use.
Language: switch Lao/Thai/English at the top corner (flags) — remembered per browser.

extraSections.title: Receiving a device (CS steps)
extraSections.intro: How CS receives a customer's device and opens a job.
items: 1) On the intake list (/service) → click “Receipt” (green button).
2) Select or add the customer: name · phone · address.
3) Choose the service type — CI (walk-in) / ST (in-warehouse) / IH (on-site) / PS (pickup then repair).
4) Enter device details: product · brand/model · SN · accessories brought.
5) Type the symptom (as reported) + attach photos (if any).
6) Pick a technician (if known) and the return method.
7) Save → get a job number → print the A4 receipt for the customer + print the 75×100 sticker for the device.

extraSections.title: FAQ
items: Scan shows “not in system”? → SN/number mismatch — try typing the job number instead of SN.
Device already returned but you want to count it? → You can; the system flags “returned” (amber).
Clicked Close·not-found by mistake? → Go to “Not-found devices (missing)” → click “Restore” → back in the queue instantly.
Want to hide “Manage backlog”? → Users → System settings → turn off “Manage backlog”.
Label doesn't fill 75×100? → When printing, choose 75×100 paper and margin = none/0.
Can I delete a receipt? → Managers only and it's irreversible — use “Cancel job” instead if you need to keep history.

extraSections.title: Installation system
extraSections.intro: Installation jobs are separate from repairs — use the “Install” menu. Technicians are assigned by tech_code and have a daily appointment queue.
items: Stages: ① Open/await-assign → ② await-accept → ③ await spare request → ④ await spare pickup → ⑤ await-install → ⑥ installing → ⑦ await-QC → ⑧ await customer feedback → ⑨ await-close.
Daily queue: My → Daily job queue — technicians see today's appointments.
Assigning: the supervisor assigns a technician (tech_code) at “Open / await-assign”.
Spares: request → pick up spares before installing; leftover spares are returned at “Return install spares”.
QC + feedback: pass QC → customer feedback → close the job.
Reports: installation report, monthly install-spares summary, customer survey (Install/Reports menu).

extraSections.title: Common installation situations
items: Customer scheduled today → tech checks the daily queue → accept → go install.
Not enough spares → request more / purchase before installing (don't go empty-handed).
Installed but customer hasn't rated → follow up at /installations/feedback.
Spares left after install → return to warehouse (WI-I05), don't leave them with the tech.
Customer reschedules → supervisor re-queues at Open / await-assign.
QC failed → tech fixes, then resubmits to QC.

extraSections.title: Tech knowledge & FAQ
extraSections.intro: Tips and common questions for repair technicians.
items: Before swapping a part: reproduce the fault + measure real values (voltage/current/resistance), don't guess.
Record the diagnosed fault (issue_2) clearly — it's evidence and helps with repeat jobs.
Photograph before/after and attach to the job — confirms condition.
Warranty: if the customer voided it, state the reason (warranty_reason) before charging.
Spares: draw only what you use; return leftovers to the warehouse — don't hold them.
Fridge/AC: check refrigerant leak + compressor before declaring unrepairable.
Washer 'won't spin': check motor/belt/board before replacing the (expensive) board.
Safety: unplug + discharge before touching the board/capacitors.
Recurring failures: check the 'repeat repairs' report — same tech/same fault?
Frequent QC fails: review the checklist before submitting.

extraSections.title: Install tech knowledge
items: AC: pipe/wire length to spec, vacuum before releasing refrigerant, leak-check.
Install level — washer/fridge/AC — to prevent vibration/standing water.
Electrical: correct breaker/ground size, don't overload.
Working at height: rope/scaffold, never alone up high.
Test after install: run it + measure + show the customer.
Clean up the site + photograph the finished work.

extraSections.title: Claim system — Repair-first
extraSections.intro: The device enters Repair first → tech checks/diagnoses → CLAIM_SIDE opens a claim. A claim hangs off the repair job (ref_job). 3 pages: /claims/shop · supplier · reimburse.
items: CLM-B shop sends to claim (/claims/shop): the master doc — created via intake ‘Receive claim item’ (/service/new?kind=claim). received→check/decide (replace/repair)→return to shop→close. Resolved at the center. Has scope (whole/part) + fulfillment (stock/purchase/supplier).
CLM-A claim spare from supplier (/claims/supplier): request a spare/replacement from the supplier while repairing. draft→send supplier(email)→review→approve→receive new→close.

CLM-C bill fee to supplier (/claims/reimburse): repair in-warranty free for the customer → collect from the supplier. Available after the device is returned. notify→notified→paid (link COB · send email · mark paid).
Open a claim from the repair job: buttons A (while repairing) / C (after return) — carries product/SN/brand/ref_job. The job list shows a ‘claim’ badge.
Guards: B received→checking only via tech QC · C paid via ‘mark paid’ · edit only at the first stage. Technicians don't create claims.
Supplier & brand come from ERP (ap_supplier / ic_brand) — brand auto from ic_inventory.item_brand.

extraSections.title: Maintenance / AC-Cleaning module
extraSections.intro: The Maintenance module handles scheduled service jobs — AC cleaning, washer-drum cleaning, fridge check-ups — not fault repairs. It is a standalone menu (it does not share the repair dashboard/pipeline) with its own stage machine derived from timestamps in ods_tb_maintenance.
items: The /maintenance home page lists all open maintenance jobs — search by code/customer/phone/technician, sortable, paginated, with an open-count badge beside the menu.
Job codes use the MC-xxx format (distinct from ordinary repair jobs). Walk-in customer name/phone/site address are stored directly on the job.

Six real stages + cancel, per maintenance-stage.ts: 0 Received / awaiting schedule+assign → 1 Awaiting technician accept → 2 Awaiting on-site cleaning → 3 Cleaning → 4 Awaiting QC → 5 Awaiting payment / close → 6 Done. (−1 = Cancelled).
The service catalog is pulled straight from the ERP (ic_inventory, code 9702%, item_type=1) — cleaning services with latest price in kip, not a seed table.
The /maintenance/status/<slug> pages are per-stage queues (receive · wait-accept · wait-clean · cleaning · wait-qc · wait-payment) — like the repair dashboard but standalone.
The /maintenance/[code] page shows details + a Timeline (time spent per stage) + a single advance button that changes with the current stage.

How it differs from repair: no goods-in to the warehouse (the technician cleans on-site — stage 2 “Awaiting on-site cleaning”), fewer stages (6 vs repair's 12), and no parts/warranty/claim involvement.
Access: every action checks MAINTENANCE_SIDE (CS/technician/supervisor). Technicians see only their own jobs (ownJobsOnly); supervisors/CS see all.

extraSections.title: Spare-parts procurement chain — SPR → WPRA → PO → WPOA
extraSections.intro: Procurement is one single document, created and tracked entirely in ERP (odg). The chain: Purchase Request (SPR) → PR approval (WPRA) → Purchase Order (PO) → PO approval (WPOA) → warehouse receipt (PUI). ODS only keeps the job's own stage (spare_order/spare_arrive); the real documents all live in ERP.
items: The Purchase Request (SPR · trans_flag 2 · doc_format 'SPR') is raised at /purchase-requests and written to ERP only — linked to the repair job via doc_ref = job code. The legacy ODS RQ (trans_flag 78) is no longer created.
An approver clicks 'Approve' at /approvals/purchase-requests to emit WPRA (trans_flag 4). No supplier is chosen yet; the job moves to stage 7 'purchasing spare parts'.

Purchasing clicks 'Issue PO' from a WPRA (/purchase-orders?tab=issue → /purchase-orders/new?from=WPRA) — this step requires supplier + negotiated price + ETA + transport + receiving warehouse + currency/VAT. PO = POT (Thai 05) / POH (Lao 00), trans_flag 6.
An approver clicks 'Approve PO' at /approvals/purchase-orders to emit WPOA (trans_flag 8) — the final gate before the supplier ships.
Warehouse receipt (PUIT/PUIH · trans_flag 12) happens in ERP; syncErpPurchase reads it, advances the job stage and notifies technician/warehouse automatically — there is no manual 'received' button.

The document page /purchase-orders/[docNo] has a statusbar top-right, an action bar whose buttons change by state + role, and linked chain documents on the side. Any SPR/WPRA/PO number redirects to the same page.
A PO can be issued directly (stock-up / rush buy) via /purchase-orders/new without an SPR (60% of real POs are this) — but it still needs WPOA approval.
Permissions: raise/withdraw SPR and issue/cancel PO = purchasing/warehouse/manager (manager · admin · stock); approve SPR (WPRA) and approve PO (WPOA) = approvers (APPROVER_SIDE).

sopDocs.title: Transfer a repair job to another service center (destination confirms receipt · job keeps its stage)
sopDocs.owner: Manager / Head technician / Stock staff (manager · headtechnical · stock)
sopDocs.purpose: Open a job at one center, then send the unit to be repaired at another center. The destination center confirms receipt itself, which moves service_center to the new center. The job does not change stage (it stays at its current stage) and the stage timer keeps running as before.
sopDocs.scope: Applies to repair intake jobs that are not yet finished (return_complete empty) on the /service/stock-count page. Supported centers: 1104 ຂົວຫຼວງ, 1206 ດອນຕີ້ວ. You cannot transfer to the center it is already at. A job can have only one pending transfer at a time.
steps: Sending side: open /service/stock-count → find the job row to transfer → click 'ປັບປຸງ' (Edit).
In the 'ປັບປຸງ' modal, in the 'ຂັ້ນ (ສະຖານະ)' (Stage) field select '📦 ໂອນໄປສ້ອມສູນອື່ນ' (Transfer to another center).
Choose 'ສູນປາຍທາງ' (Destination center) — 1104 ຂົວຫຼວງ or 1206 ດອນຕີ້ວ — and type 'ເຫດຜົນ' (Reason), at least 3 characters.
Click 'ບັນທຶກ' (Save) → the system opens the transfer (received_at empty = in transit), logs to chatter, and the job stays at its current stage.
Receiving side (destination center): when the unit arrives, open /service/stock-count → find the same job → click 'ປັບປຸງ' (Edit).

sopDocs.purpose: Run spare-parts procurement through the full chain SPR → WPRA → PO → WPOA → receipt, with the real documents in ERP only and traceable back to the job at every stage.
sopDocs.scope: Repair jobs (tb_product) and installation jobs (INST-) at stage 5 where ERP stock is short. Excludes direct stock-up POs (see /purchase-orders/new).
steps: Warehouse/Purchasing: open /purchase-requests → 'jobs to purchase' section (stage-5 jobs short on ERP stock, not yet requested) → open one, enter a price per line, pick the branch (00 head office / 05 Odien Thai), then submit to emit the SPR.
The system redirects straight to /purchase-orders/[SPR] — statusbar on 'Purchase request', awaiting an approver.
Approver: /approvals/purchase-requests, 'Waiting' tab → click 'Approve' → confirm → WPRA is emitted. Job enters stage 7 'purchasing spare parts'.

Purchasing: /purchase-orders shows a 'WPRA waiting to issue PO' banner → click → /purchase-orders/new?from=WPRA → choose supplier, enter negotiated prices, ETA, transport, receiving warehouse, currency/VAT and cash/credit terms → issue the PO (POT/POH).

Tracking: /purchase-orders (status filters waiting / approved / received + document-age column, long waits in red) or open any document page for the full statusbar.

wiDocs.title: Record payment & track outstanding debt
wiDocs.purpose: Record incoming repair payments and track outstanding debt. The ods_service_payment table is the single source where incoming money is recorded (the old SIN receipts are all 0.00 and unusable).
wiDocs.scope: The /reports/service-debts page is visible only to [M, A]. For front-desk CS collecting cash, the manager grants access per person.
steps: Go to /reports/service-debts. Debt = quotes the customer has accepted (trans_flag=17, aprove_status=1, aprove_status_2=1) minus what has been paid.

Use the filters: customer type (all/shop/general/unset) and scope (due / all), then click 'Filter'. The summary tiles at top (jobs/quoted/received/due) are computed across all rows, not just this page.

ⓘ Note: jobs before 2026-07-17 have no payment records ⇒ they all show as 'due' even if paid in cash. Do NOT auto-backfill — record each one manually. Red rows 'returned but unpaid' are the highest risk.
Take payment: click 'Receive money' on a row (shown only when due>0 and you have update rights). The dialog opens with the amount preset to the full due.

Enter: amount (overwrite for partial payment), date (not after today), method (cash/transfer/other), reference, note → Save. recordServicePayment computes 'due' on the server and cannot accept more than the outstanding amount (one typo = wrong ledger).
On save it logs to the job timeline (received X THB · Y still due / fully paid) and /reports/service-debts totals refresh.
Wrong entry: it can be reversed (undoServicePayment) — not deleted silently but logged on the timeline with the reversed amount. Same rights as recording.
Set customer type (setCustomerKind) from the /customers table (shop/general) — used to split /reports/service-by-kind.
Related reports: /reports/service-revenue (by month, counted by quote date), /reports/service-by-kind (split by customer type, counted by intake date).

wiDocs.title: Hold / reject a job (hold & reject)
wiDocs.purpose: Flag jobs the queue can't move (hold) so the stage clock stops and they split off to a 'problem' tab; and let a technician reject a not-yet-accepted job with a reason.
wiDocs.scope: hold/release = supervisor/approver (APPROVER_SIDE M, HT). reject = technician (TECH_SIDE M, HT, T). The server always re-checks.
steps: Hold a job: open /service/{code}. If permitted you'll see HoldButtons with 3 outcomes — ① 'Needs check' ② 'Cancel' ③ 'Repaired'. All require a reason ≥ 3 chars.

① 'Needs check' → holdJob: raises a 'problem' flag (kind=other), stops the stage clock, moves the job to the 'problem' tab. The flag does not change the stage and does not remove it from 'open jobs'. 1 job = 1 open flag (can't flag twice).
⚠️ The 'flag problem job' capability must be enabled at /manage/settings (SETTING.JOB_HOLD) first — if off, holdJob returns an error.
Release the flag: on /service/{code} a flagged job shows a 'Needs check · X days' badge + an Undo button → releaseJobHold. The clock resumes from where it stopped (not restarted).

③ 'Repaired' → markJobRepaired: supervisor override for stuck jobs (stage 6 waiting for parts can't use finishRepairFlow). Sets time_finish_repair + status=5 ⇒ the job goes to the QC/return stage (not skipped) and its hold is auto-released.
② 'Cancel' → requestCancel: enters the cancellation approval queue /approvals/cancellations (does not delete the job).

Reject a job: a technician who hasn't accepted clicks 'Decline' (at /installations/accept for installs; on the repair side technicians mainly use the mobile app). A reason ≥ 3 chars is required in the modal, then 'Confirm decline'.

rejectJobAction → rejectJob: allowed only while not yet accepted / not started (repair: repair_confirm null + stage 1; install: stage 1). Once accepted or parts requested, it can't be rejected (contact CS to reassign).
After rejection: the job returns to the assignment queue (technician cleared), the reason is stored in ods_job_reject, and CS (admin/manager) is notified immediately.

wiDocs.title: Service notices

steps: Go to /service/notices — the list of notices not yet intaken (no tb_product.ref_notice points to them yet). Search/sort/paginate 20 rows/page.
Read columns: code, notify date-time, notifier, phone, product, SN, customer, initial symptom, remark, image ('View image' loads on click).

Intake: click 'Open job' → /service/notices/{code}. The ServiceNoticeForm pulls category/brand/technician from ERP, and if ref_code+doc_ref/SN exist it matches the source invoice (item_code, category, invoice date).
Fill/confirm the data and save = convert into an intake receipt for repair. If the notice was already intaken, the page auto-redirects to /service/{code}.

Delete a notice: click the delete button (NoticeDeleteButton) → deleteNotice. A notice that has already opened a job cannot be deleted (server blocks it: intake receipt #… references ref_notice). Deletion is logged with who did it.
ⓘ You can delete a notice only — deleting a job (tb_product) is still strictly forbidden.
Notices come from 2 paths: the public form /report-repair (customer, no login) and /sales/report-repair (sales, see SOP-R10).

wiDocs.title: Manage customer data
wiDocs.purpose: Add/edit/delete customer records (ar_customer) and set the type (shop/general) correctly for intake receipts and reports.
wiDocs.scope: All of /customers = SERVICE_SIDE (M, A). Table ar_customer columns address/city/provine ('provine' is misspelled but is the real column — do not change).
steps: Go to /customers — the customer list (search code/name/phone/address, sort, paginate 20/page). The 'intake receipts' column counts only the 20 people on this page.
Set type from the row: the 'Type' cell (KindCell) select shop/general → saves immediately (setCustomerKind, no confirm button, reversible). Used by /reports/service-by-kind.

Add: /customers/new → CustomerForm (next code auto-filled). Name* (name_1) required; name_2, address, province, city, phone. Save → createCustomer (pg_advisory lock prevents duplicate codes) → back to /customers?ok=saved.
Edit: click the edit icon → /customers/{code}/edit. Change name/address/province/city/phone → updateCustomer → /customers?ok=edited. This page has a Chatter (change history).
Delete: click DeleteButton → deleteCustomer. Cannot delete if an intake receipt (tb_product) or install job (ods_tb_install) references it → shows 'in use'.
ⓘ The old ods edit_cust wrote to the wrong table ⇒ never saved; here it correctly uses ar_customer.

wiDocs.title: Approve PR / PO (approver buttons)
wiDocs.purpose: Describe the steps and buttons an approver uses to approve purchase requests (SPR to WPRA) and purchase orders (PO to WPOA), plus how to undo a wrong approval.
wiDocs.scope: Pages /approvals/purchase-requests, /approvals/purchase-orders and the document page /purchase-orders/[docNo]. Available only to APPROVER_SIDE roles.
steps: Approve PR: go to /approvals/purchase-requests, 'Waiting' tab → click 'Approve' on the row (opens the document page) or click the SPR number to open /purchase-orders/[SPR] directly.

On the document page (statusbar 'Purchase request'): click 'Approve' → confirm 'Approve request?' → WPRA is emitted (no supplier needed yet). To reject, click 'Reject' → the SPR is deleted from ERP and the job returns to spare-parts handling.

Wrong approval (approved but PO not yet issued): on the document page in the 'Approved' state, click 'Undo approval' (deletes WPRA, doc returns to 'Waiting') or 'Delete whole request' (deletes SPR+WPRA). Once a PO exists this is blocked — the server names the blocking PO.

Approve PO: go to /approvals/purchase-orders, 'Waiting' tab → click 'Approve PO' on the row → confirm 'Approve purchase order?' → WPOA is emitted. (An 'Approve PO' button also exists on the /purchase-orders list.)
Before approving a PO, check the 'Document info' block on the page: supplier, total, ETA, currency/VAT (exclusive/inclusive) and payment (cash / credit N days + due date).

Cancel an approved PO (not yet received): approvers only — click 'Cancel', give a reason → PO + WPOA are deleted from ERP. If it has been received (a PUI exists) it cannot be cancelled — return the goods in ERP instead.
